subject: PO line-item granularity, invoice cadence & net terms — Greentech pilot
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@greentech.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Davenport <mark.davenport@greentech.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PO & invoicing format for pilot — line-item requirement

Diego —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has a couple of non-negotiable asks before we can route a PO:

- PO must include line-item granularity (ERP requires each SKU mapped to a PO line with a unique reference).
- Invoices need to be produced weekly with a running statement (we'd like to see week-start/week-end and PO line references).
- Standard terms are Net45; exceptions for Net30 require early-pay triggers documented.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) Accept a blanket PO with line-item references (vs one PO per invoice).
2) Produce weekly invoices tied to PO line references.
3) Offer an early-pay discount (our AP team prefers a small percent for Net30).

I've attached our PO template and the procurement form you requested. Let me know if you need a stub or example of our ERP mapping.

Attachments: Greentech_PO_Template.xlsx, Procurement_Form_Greentech.pdf

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Procurement Manager
Greentech Solutions
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@greentech.com>
Cc: Mark Davenport <mark.davenport@greentech.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO & invoicing format for pilot — line-item requirement

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: yes (with options), yes (we can produce weekly statements), and we can propose a tiered early-pay concession. A couple of follow ups so we can lock an approach that doesn't create reconciliation overhead for either side:

- Blanket PO vs per-invoice PO: we typically accept a blanket/master PO and reference your line-item IDs on each invoice. That avoids issuing many POs while still satisfying ERP matching.
- Weekly invoice cadence: we can emit weekly invoices and include a CSV with PO_line_id, SKU, quantity, unit_price, and Redwood invoice line reference. That CSV is intended to be machine-ingestible for your AP team.
- Early-pay discounts: finance prefers defining either (A) a 1% discount for payment within 15 days (Net15) or (B) 1.5% for payment within 30 days (Net30) if a preauthorized budget is in place.

Can you confirm whether Greentech requires the PO_line_id to be embedded in the invoice line or if a separate PO-to-invoice mapping file is OK? Also, do you have a preferred file layout for the CSV (column order) or should we use our standard invoice-export schema?

I attached our SOW and a short invoicing SLA so procurement can see the fields we plan to emit. If you prefer, we can stand up a one-off sample invoice next week against your PO template to validate ingestion.

Next steps I propose:
- Procurement sends back a completed sample PO (fills in a single blanket PO row with 3–4 sample PO_line_ids).
- We generate a sample weekly invoice + CSV for your AP to ingest.
- Confirm early-pay discount level for commercial paperwork.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf, Redwood_Invoicing_SLA.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: PO & invoicing format for pilot — finance view

Vanessa / Diego —

Finance note: Net45 is our standard for new accounts. We can approve an early-pay concession programmatically if Greentech provides a preauthorized PO or a payment commitment schedule (i.e., locked-in spend threshold). Suggested structure:

- Standard: Net45, weekly invoices.
- Early-pay offer: 1% discount if paid within 15 days OR 1.5% if paid within 30 days, but only if a blanket PO with preauthorized spend (minimum monthly commitment) is provided.

I'll approve the 1.5% Net30 if Legal signs off on the clause and the Sales Ops entry includes the PO_id mapping. Otherwise, stick to 1% for Net15 as a lower-risk option.

Ben
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@greentech.com>
Cc: Mark Davenport <mark.davenport@greentech.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed invoicing workflow & commercial concession

Priya —

Thanks — based on internal alignment here's a concrete proposal to keep your AP team happy while minimizing reconciliation work: 

1) PO model: Greentech issues a blanket/master PO referencing line-item IDs. Each weekly invoice will include a column with the matching PO_line_id for each billed SKU. That satisfies a three-way match on your side.

2) Invoice cadence & format: weekly invoices (Mon-Sun) with a machine-readable CSV attachment: columns = [invoice_id, invoice_date, po_id, po_line_id, sku, qty, unit_price, line_total, redwood_line_ref]. PDF invoice will follow the CSV for human review.

3) Net terms & early-pay: Standard Net45. Commercial concession: 1.5% discount if paid within 30 days (Net30) provided Greentech:
   - supplies a preauthorized blanket PO with a minimum monthly spend baseline, and
   - signs the invoicing SLA (attached).

4) Implementation steps & timeline:
   - Priya: send a completed sample blanket PO (a single PO with 3 sample PO_line_ids) — target: end of this week.
   - Redwood: generate a sample weekly invoice + CSV and share by next Tuesday for your AP to test.
   - Contract: we will add an early-pay clause to the order form referencing the agreed discount and preauth condition. Legal review should be lightweight.

If that sounds good I can open a HubSpot task and a DocuSign envelope for the order form.
